column1: # The touch panels this device is laid out for, one per device tree compatible.
# Installed at /usr/lib/nullroute/panels.tsv. The kiosk reads it at start to
# choose the scale it draws at (chromium-for-panel), and the layout checks read
# it to choose the sizes they measure every screen at
# (tools/checks/check-screen-fit.mjs, tools/checks/check-journeys.mjs). One
# table, so the size a screen is measured at and the size it is drawn at on the
# panel cannot drift apart.
# A panel is matched by the compatible string of its node in the running device
# tree, which is what the overlay named in config.txt put there. Two of these
# have the same pixels and differ only in size (Touch Display 2 at 5 and 7
# inches), so pixels alone cannot choose the scale.
# scale: device pixels per CSS pixel. Chosen so a CSS pixel is 0.15 to 0.19 mm
# on the glass, the range phones use, which makes the 44 pixel target every
# control is held to 6.4 to 8.4 mm. The viewport a screen is laid out in is
# pixels divided by scale, rounded down: 800x480, 480x853, 360x640, 360x601.
# The HyperPixel is at 1.33 rather than 1.5. At 1.5 it is 320 pixels wide, and
# the passphrase keyboard needs 6 keys of 44 pixels and their gaps in a row,
# which with the body's margins is 324 of 296. 1.33 makes it 360.9 by 601.5,
# the width of the 5 inch panel with a fraction to spare, so no rounding in the
# browser can put it a pixel under the 360 the interface refuses to draw below.
# A CSS pixel is then 0.146 mm.
# Columns are separated by one tab. Lines starting with # are comments.
# compatible
raspberrypi,7inch-touchscreen-panel
